why: Drops the refusal, so an --only id matching no entry runs whatever else was named and reports a clean sweep of it. This is the pre-#529 hazard in its worst form: one typo among four ids costs three quarters of the work with nothing on screen saying so. A run either honours everything asked of it or stops.
killedBy: selectOnly / missingOnlyReport still refuses a SINGLE unmatched id, naming it -- the pre-#529 property the multi-id case must not lose
